findings.description: The bucket is explicitly noted as public and lacks any server-side encryption configuration, ACL restriction, or versioning, exposing customer data (including the uploaded customer-master.xlsx object) to unauthenticated public access and leaving stored data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects are stored unencrypted by default rather than protected with SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS.
A file named customer-master.xlsx, likely containing sensitive customer data, is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing confidential data.
The bucket has a private ACL but no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving financial data stored unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has versioning enabled but no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving operational data unencrypted at rest.
The bucket has versioning and access logging configured but lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving data science data unencrypted at rest.
